preamble: Retroflexion of the palato-alveolar affricate [tʃ] to the retroflex [ʈʂ] occurred in Polish, where Proto-Slavic *č [tʃ] became the retroflex (flat postalveolar) cz [ʈʂ] that contrasts with alveolo-palatal ć [tɕ]. In Mayan, Wikipedia's Proto-Mayan article, citing Campbell (1997: 164), describes a chain shift in Mamean in which *r became [t], *t became [tʃ], *tʃ became [tʂ] and *ʃ became [ʂ], and says the retroflex affricates and fricatives later diffused into Qʼanjobʼalan. In Kaufman & Justeson's (2003) Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary, cognate sets with *ch have tx in Mam, Tektitek, Awakatek and Ixil and in Qʼanjobʼal, Akatek and Poptiʼ, while Kʼicheʼan, Yucatecan, Chuj, Tojolabʼal and Mochoʼ keep ch: *chuun 'lime' is Ixil txun beside Kʼicheʼ chuun, and Proto-Mayan *chiim 'net bag' is Qʼanjobʼal txim beside Chuj chim. Forms are cited in the dictionary's spelling, in which 7 is the glottal stop. In the ALMG convention for these languages ch is [tʃ] and tx is [tʂ] (Wikipedia, Mayan languages), and Wikipedia's Mam and Qʼanjobʼal articles list tx as [ʈ͡ʂ] or [ʈʂ]. Not every set has tx throughout: Tektitek has chkup 'animal' and chimb'il 'morral, matate', Tacaná Mam has yooch 'escalera' beside yootx elsewhere in Mam, the Greater Qʼanjobʼalan set *chanh 'skirt' has ch in Qʼanjobʼal chan, Akatek chaaneh and Poptiʼ chanh-e, while Kaufman's own entries for Qʼanjobʼal and Poptiʼ 'urine' read ch/txul (check), though the OKMA forms Qʼanjobʼal txulej, Akatek txuleh and Poptiʼ hatxule have tx (p. 355). Conversely, Chuj, which otherwise keeps ch, is listed with both b'utx and b'uch 'nixtamal'.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Mayan *ch to Mamean (Mam, Tektitek, Awakatek, Ixil)

examples.to: Mam txu7 'teta(s), chiche(s), pecho(s)', Tektitek ntxu7un 'mamó'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 377); 7 is the glottal stop. Poptiʼ has xtxutxwi 'mamó'; Mochoʼ chu7 'mamar' keeps ch.

examples.to: Tektitek txun, Mam txuun, Awakatek txuun, Ixil txun 'cal'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 527), set labelled EM (proto-Eastern Mayan). The Mam form is from San Ildefonso Ixtahuacán (Kaufman's MAMi); Tacaná, Ostuncalco and Cajolá Mam (MAMt, MAMo, MAMc) have txun. Kaqchikel chun and Qʼeqchiʼ chun keep ch.

examples.to: Tektitek txil, Mam txiil, Awakatek txiil 'grillo'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 689), set labelled pCM (proto Central Mayan). Chuj chilich and Poqomchiʼ chili7 also keep ch.

examples.to: Mam txkup, Awakatek txuk, Ixil txokop 'animal'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 592), set labelled EM. Mam txkup is from Tacaná, Ostuncalco and San Ildefonso Ixtahuacán (MAMt, MAMo, MAMi); Cajolá Mam (MAMc) has txuk. Tektitek has chkup, with ch.

examples.to: Mam yootx, Awakatek yootx, Ixil yotx 'escalera'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 942), set labelled EM; word-final *ch. Mam yootx is from Ostuncalco, Cajolá and San Ildefonso Ixtahuacán (MAMo, MAMc, MAMi); Tacaná Mam (MAMt) has yooch. Sipakapense has yoch.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Mayan *ch to Qʼanjobʼal, Akatek and Poptiʼ

examples.from: Proto-Mayan *chiim 'net bag' (Chuj chim 'red', Yukatek chim 'bolsa', Kʼicheʼ chiim 'morral, matate')
examples.to: Qʼanjobʼal txim 'red', Akatek txim 'red de pita grande', Poptiʼ txim 'red, bolsa'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 977). Tektitek has chimb'il 'morral, matate', with ch.

examples.to: Qʼanjobʼal txikin, Akatek txikin-eh, Poptiʼ txikin 'oreja'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 271), set labelled WM (proto Western Mayan).
Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 980), set labelled WM+. Awakatek has mo7tx; Tzeltal moch keeps ch.

examples.to: Qʼanjobʼal, Akatek, Poptiʼ b'utx 'nixtamal, maíz cocido'
examples.note: Kaufman & Justeson (2003: 1222), set labelled EM+GQ (Eastern Mayan and Greater Qʼanjobʼalan). Mam, Tektitek and Awakatek have b'uutx; Chuj is listed with both b'utx and b'uch.

sources: Kaufman, T., with Justeson, J. (2003). A Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary. FAMSI.
